description:
Inspect and refactor client-server synchronization to eliminate latency and state discrepancies:
- Address stale client-side overwrites where mutation responses overwrite updated subscription states.
- Evaluate pushing fully updated aim/phase payloads in WebSocket events instead of triggering client-side query round-trips.
- Investigate parallelizing server-side file listing to speed up full-project loads.
- Explore sequence numbers/versions for resource atoms to prevent out-of-order updates.
reflection: Completed the client/server synchronization refactor across all four requested areas. (1) Monotonic per-resource revisions prevent delayed aim and phase mutation/fetch responses from overwriting fresher subscription state, with explicit race regressions. (2) Central aim/phase writes now emit optional full entity payloads; the frontend applies payloads directly without query round-trips while ID-only deletion/compatibility events retain the fetch fallback, and redundant post-write notifications were removed. (3) Active/archive aim listing, phase enumeration, and loop-target discovery read independent JSON files concurrently while preserving deterministic order and malformed-file isolation. (4) The revision atoms provide the requested out-of-order protection. Verification: focused MultiClient 5/5, full frontend 215/215, backend 68/68, frontend vue-tsc, backend tsc, and git diff checks all pass.

status.comment: All synchronization-refactor clauses are implemented and internally verified; awaiting user acceptance.
